issues.quote: Commits form one because a commit can name two parents, when two lines of work are joined again
issues.text: git-commit-tree: "A commit object may have any number of parents... Having more than one parent makes the commit a merge between several lines of history." 'two' reads as the maximum; the ledger (claim 4) already says 'more than one'. Not wrong, only narrower than the docs. Same wording in summary line 2 and q6 explanation c.
issues.fix: Section 4: 'because a commit can name two or more parents, when lines of work are joined again'. Summary line 2: 'a commit can name more than one parent'. q6 explanation c (en/vi): 'one commit can name two or more parents' / 'một commit có thể gọi tên hai parent trở lên'.

issues.quote: With `--graph` each `*` is one commit; the second `...` below hides the four older ones.
issues.text: 'The second `...`' made me look for what the first one hides; that is only answered three paragraphs later (the `##` line). I paused and scrolled down to check I was reading the output right.
issues.fix: Add to this sentence: 'the first `...` hides a line explained at the end of this section'.

issues.text: The prose says `git show --stat` 'lists the files the newest commit changed', but not what `14`, the row of `+` and 'insertions' mean. I guessed 14 added lines; the misconception bullet later leans on this output, so a word would help.
issues.fix: Add to the `git show --stat` sentence: 'with the number of lines added (`+`) or removed (`-`) in each'.

issues.quote: In the example system you run `git-playground/build-history.sh`, which builds a throwaway repository
issues.text: Here I run `build-history.sh` and then work 'inside it', but Try it runs `inspect-commit.sh`, which builds the playground by itself. I was unsure whether I must run `build-history.sh` myself first, and where (laptop or lab box).
issues.fix: Add half a sentence saying the script runs in the lab box and that `inspect-commit.sh` in Try it runs it for you.

issues.quote: A graph is commits joined by parent arrows, where two arrows may leave one commit or arrive at it. Commits form one because a commit can name two parents, when two lines of work are joined again, and two commits can name the same parent
issues.text: I read this twice to map 'two arrows leave one commit' to 'two parents' and 'arrive at it' to 'two commits naming the same parent'. The ideas are all there; the order of the two cases just flips between the sentences.
issues.fix: Say the two cases in the same order in both sentences, or add '(two parents)' and '(two children)' after 'leave' and 'arrive at'.

issues.text: Neither this lesson nor the terminal-basics summary tells me how to see whether the lab box is up, or what `scripts/up.sh` prints. I would just run it anyway, so this does not stop me.
